seoTitle: How to Sync Etsy With QuickBooks Online
metaDescription: Connect Etsy to QuickBooks Online with the Etsy Connector app so sales, fees, and customer data flow into your books automatically.
intro: Etsy doesn't hand off sales data to QuickBooks Online on its own — the connection runs through an app called Etsy Connector by QuickBooks, installed from QuickBooks' own integrations panel. Once it's linked, every invoice created in Etsy turns into a sales receipt or invoice in QuickBooks automatically, with matching customer and product records, so you stop retyping order totals into a spreadsheet at the end of every week. This guide walks through finding the connector, understanding what it actually does before you install it, and what changes in your books once it's running.

steps.heading: Open My integrations from the QuickBooks dashboard
steps.body: From your QuickBooks Online home screen, open the integrations panel in the top corner — it lists apps already connected to your account (things like Bill, the Wix Connector, or Zapier show up here if you've used them) alongside an "Explore integrations" link for adding new ones. This is also where an "Enhanced" section highlights featured partner apps, so it's worth a glance even beyond the one you're installing today. Etsy isn't listed among the defaults, which is exactly why you need to search for it rather than expecting it to appear automatically.

image.caption: The My integrations panel from the QuickBooks Online dashboard, showing already-connected apps and a link to explore more.

steps.heading: Find the Etsy Connector by QuickBooks listing
steps.body: Searching from Explore integrations surfaces "Etsy Connector by QuickBooks," built by Intuit and rated in the hundreds of reviews. The Overview tab opens with three key benefits up front: it shares data automatically between Etsy and QuickBooks Online, keeps invoices current without manual entry, and cuts down the human error that comes from copying numbers by hand. A screenshot on the listing itself shows what the synced transactions eventually look like inside QuickBooks, which is a useful preview before you commit to installing anything.

image.caption: The Etsy Connector by QuickBooks listing page, with its key benefits and a preview of synced transaction data.

steps.heading: Read what the connector actually automates
steps.body: Scrolling the same listing down to "How it works with QuickBooks" and "Details" spells out the mechanics: the connector shares data whenever an invoice is made in Etsy, creating a matching sales invoice or receipt in QuickBooks Online, and it creates the associated products and customers along the same pass. It also lets you review all imported Etsy data for correctness before it's finalized, sends payment records from Etsy through to QuickBooks, and offers a variety of import settings so you can control exactly how that data lands in your books rather than accepting a one-size-fits-all mapping.

image.caption: The connector's How it works and Details sections, listing exactly what syncs automatically once it's connected.

steps.heading: Click Get integration now and authorize both accounts
steps.body: The green "Get integration now" button in the top corner starts the install. You'll be prompted to sign in to your Etsy seller account and grant the connector permission to read your shop's orders, then confirm which QuickBooks Online company file it should sync into if you manage more than one. This step is the only place real account credentials are involved, so make sure you're doing it from Etsy's and Intuit's own login screens rather than a third-party page.

steps.heading: Set your import preferences before the first sync
steps.body: Before transactions start flowing, go through the connector's import settings and decide how Etsy fees should be categorized, whether historical orders should be pulled in or only new ones going forward, and which QuickBooks accounts sales and shipping income should post to. Getting this right up front saves a cleanup pass later — miscategorized fees are one of the most common issues sellers run into after connecting an e-commerce platform to their books.

steps.heading: Review the first batch of synced transactions
steps.body: After the initial sync, open QuickBooks and check that a handful of recent Etsy orders appear as sales receipts or invoices with the right customer, product, and amount. The connector's review feature lets you catch mismatches — a product that didn't map cleanly, or a customer created twice — while the volume is still small, rather than discovering the problem three months and hundreds of orders later.

steps.heading: Let it run and check in periodically
steps.body: Once the first batch looks clean, the connector keeps working in the background, turning new Etsy invoices into QuickBooks records without further action from you. Still, it's worth a monthly glance at your Profit & Loss and Sales reports to confirm the numbers make sense against what you know about your shop's actual order volume — automation reduces manual entry errors, but it doesn't replace a periodic sanity check on the totals.

faq.question: What data syncs between Etsy and QuickBooks Online?
faq.answer: The Etsy Connector creates a sales invoice or receipt in QuickBooks for every Etsy order, along with the matching product and customer records, and it can also send payment data from Etsy through to QuickBooks.

faq.question: Is the Etsy Connector a native QuickBooks feature or a separate app?
faq.answer: It's a separate app, built by Intuit and listed in QuickBooks Online's integrations marketplace — you install it from there rather than finding it in QuickBooks' default settings.

faq.question: Does syncing Etsy with QuickBooks reduce bookkeeping errors?
faq.answer: Yes. Automating the transfer of sales, fee, and customer data removes most of the manual re-entry that causes mismatched totals, though it's still worth spot-checking the first batch of synced orders.

faq.question: Can I control how Etsy data gets categorized in QuickBooks?
faq.answer: Yes. The connector provides import settings so you can choose how fees, income, and historical orders map into your QuickBooks accounts before the first sync runs.

faq.question: Is this integration suitable for a seller with no bookkeeping background?
faq.answer: Yes. The install runs through a guided flow from QuickBooks' own integrations panel, and the connector's review step lets you check that Etsy orders came through correctly before relying on the synced numbers.
